neutral_facts.value: The accused were part of an unlawful assembly that surrounded and assaulted the deceased, preventing his escape. The initial assault was made on the head of the deceased with a lathi by one of the accused. The deceased fell down and was further assaulted by two persons with spears. Another accused assaulted a witness on the head with a lathi, causing injuries. Both the deceased and the witness were taken to the hospital where their injuries were examined. The police officer-in-charge stated that he requested injury reports for the witnesses, which were made available before the charge sheet was submitted. The prosecution relied on the eyewitness accounts of the injured witnesses and the police officer's statements to establish the occurrence and the injuries sustained.

key_evidence_accepted.value: The Supreme Court accepted the ocular evidence of the injured witnesses P.W. 7 and 8, their statements recorded at the hospital, and the testimony of P.W. 11, the officer-in-charge of the police station.

witness_credibility.value: The court assessed the credibility of the injured witnesses P.W. 7 and 8 based on their oral evidence, their statements recorded at the hospital, and the testimony of P.W. 11, noting that the absence of injury reports was a defective investigation but did not discredit their credibility as injured witnesses.

quotes.text: The fact that there was no injury report, can at best be classified as a defective investigation but cannot raise doubts about the credibility of their being injured witnesses in the same occurrence

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the charge under Section 147 was defective because it was framed against only four persons and not all six accused, without the aid of Sections 141 and 146. They also claimed that the evidence of the injured witnesses P.W. 7 and 8 was credible despite the absence of injury reports, and that the appellants were part of an unlawful assembly with a common object of murdering the deceased.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the charge under Section 147 was defective and that the appellants were seriously prejudiced in their defence because the questions put to them under Section 313 were inadequate and perfunctory, denying them the opportunity to present their defence. They also claimed that the absence of injury reports for P.W. 7 and 8 cast doubt on the credibility of the prosecution's case.

defence_argument.note: no quote occurs in the judgment; closest passage (p.7, match 73): "All relevant questions with regard to the accus ations were not put to the appellants, denying them the opportunity to present their defence."

legal_principle_applied.value: The court applied the principle of audi alteram partem under Section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, which provides the accused with an opportunity to explain circumstances appearing against them in the evidence. The court also emphasized that the absence of prejudice must be demonstrated for any challenge to the trial process.

quotes.text: Section 313, Cr.P.C. incorporates the principle of audi alteram partem. It provides an opportunity to the accused for his defence by making him aware fully of the prosecution allegations against him and to answer the same in support of his innocence.
